description: Comprehensive Hierarchical Curriculum Schema across A1-C2 Levels with detailed grammar, units, and communicative functional objectives.

levels.global_scale_descriptor: Can understand and use familiar everyday expressions and very basic phrases aimed at the satisfaction of needs of a concrete type.

units.title: Introductions and Personal Details
functional_objectives: Introduce oneself and others
Ask and answer questions about personal details (place of residence, people known, things owned)
grammar: Subject pronouns (I, you, he, she, it, we, they)
Possessive adjectives (my, your, his, her, its, our, their)
Question words (What, Who, Where, How old)

units.title: Everyday Life and Routines
functional_objectives: Describe daily habits and routines
State times, days of the week, and dates

units.title: My World (Family, Home, and Objects)
functional_objectives: Describe family members and relationship statuses
Identify and describe common household items and rooms

levels.global_scale_descriptor: Can understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance (e.g. very basic personal and family information, shopping, local geography, employment).

units.title: Past Events and Life Experiences
functional_objectives: Talk about past events, weekend activities, and historic events
Describe a simple biography or personal timeline
grammar: Past simple regular and irregular verbs
Past time expressions (yesterday, last week, ago)

units.title: Shopping, Fashion, and Preferences
functional_objectives: Make purchases in a shop, ask for prices, sizes, and colors
Compare items and express personal preferences
grammar: Countable and uncountable nouns (much, many, a lot of)

units.title: Travel, Directions, and Future Intentions
functional_objectives: Ask for and give directions in a city
Discuss immediate holiday plans or future arrangements
grammar: Modals of ability and permission (can, could)

levels.global_scale_descriptor: Can understand the main points of clear standard input on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, school, leisure, etc.

units.title: Life Changes and Experiences
functional_objectives: Describe life events connecting the past to the present moment
Talk about open-ended duration of actions
grammar: For and since, ever and never, just, already, yet

units.title: Rules, Advice, and Speculation
functional_objectives: Express strong obligations and prohibitions in professional and social spaces
Give constructive advice and make predictions
grammar: Modals of obligation/prohibition (must, have to, mustn't, don't have to)

units.title: Stories and Processes
functional_objectives: Narrate a cohesive story or describe a historical chain of events
Explain a mechanical process or workflow where the actor is unknown
grammar: Passive voice (present simple and past simple profiles)

levels.global_scale_descriptor: Can understand the main ideas of complex text on both concrete and abstract topics, including technical discussions in their field of specialization.

units.title: Hypothetical Scenarios and Regrets
functional_objectives: Speculate on imaginary present scenarios and evaluate alternatives
Express regret about past actions and decisions
grammar: Past modals of deduction (must have, might have, couldn't have)

units.title: Reporting Actions and Advanced Passives
functional_objectives: Report conversations, interviews, or professional statements with precise nuance
Describe systemic processes and formal societal changes
grammar: Reported speech with complex backshifts and reporting verbs (deny, insist, blame)
Passive voice across all standard tenses (including progressive and perfect)

units.title: Complex Relationships and Continuous Actions
functional_objectives: Clarify intricate conditions under which an event can occur
Describe actions that will be ongoing or completed by a future benchmark
grammar: Relative clauses (defining and non-defining) using whom/whose
Conditionals without 'if' (provided that, as long as, unless)

levels.global_scale_descriptor: Can understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts, and recognize implicit meaning. Can express ideas fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions.

units.title: Emphasis, Focus, and Structural Inversion
functional_objectives: Deliver high-impact, persuasive professional presentations
Shift structural focus to highlight critical data points or strategic ideas
grammar: Negative and restrictive inversion (e.g., 'Not only did they...', 'Seldom have we...')
Cleft sentences (It-clefts and Wh-clefts for emphasis)
Fronting and inversion with prepositional phrases

units.title: Nuanced Speculation and Compound Conditions
functional_objectives: Formulate complex hypotheses spanning across distinct timelines
Express speculative actions that were close to completion but interrupted
grammar: Advanced modals of past probability (e.g., 'should have been working')
Inverted conditional structures avoiding 'if' (e.g., 'Had we known...', 'Were they to...')

units.title: Complex Discourse and Noun Phrases
functional_objectives: Author precise academic or complex regulatory literature
Summarize massive data streams into tightly compacted professional text summaries
grammar: Advanced nominalization and complex noun phrases
Participle clauses (Present, Past, and Perfect participle clauses)
Sophisticated discourse markers for concession and cohesion

levels.global_scale_descriptor: Can understand with ease virtually everything heard or read. Can summarize information from different spoken and written sources, reconstructing arguments and accounts in a coherent presentation.

units.title: Stylistic Formality and Subjunctive Nuance
functional_objectives: Incorporate formal, legal, and highly institutional grammar variations into official text profiles
Assert crucial operational mandates, professional demands, and strategic imperatives with exact tone control
grammar: The formulaic and analytical subjunctive mood (e.g., 'It is imperative that he fulfill...', 'Be that as it may...')
Advanced modal blending and peripheral modal verbs (dare, need, ought)
Archaic and highly formal connective adverbs

units.title: Rhetorical Elasticity and Metaphorical Grammar
functional_objectives: Manipulate grammatical tense constraints to deliver precise rhetorical, literary, or ironic impact
Deploy structural syntax to convey emotional detours, understated humor, or profound emphasis
grammar: Rhetorical and metaphorical use of tenses (e.g., 'distancing present', past tenses for immediate future deadlines)
